answer: One concrete defence is a per-window score cap tied to account age. Each identity only accrues credits after passing a ramp, so at the first dawn of a new key the ceiling is tiny. An operator who manufactures a ripple of clones gets thousands of fresh accounts whose caps are all low, and merging them cannot compound anything: payouts stay capped per identity, not per swarm. Meanwhile each clone must still buy a distinct attestation, and peers flag a prism of identical phrasing as one actor. Cost scales linearly with fakes while yield stays flat.
